Automated Libra is a South African-based freejacking group that primarily targets cloud platforms offering limited-time trials of cloud resources in order to perform their cryptomining operations.

Source: Palo Alto

values.description: DragonForce operates a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) affiliate program using two ransomware variants: LockBit 3.0 and a modified ContiV3. The group uses double extortion tactics, encrypting data and threatening to leak it unless paid. Launched in June 2024, the program offers affiliates 80% of ransoms and tools to manage attacks. Affiliates can customize ransomware, disable security, and set encryption parameters. DragonForce employs the BYOVD technique to disable security processes and erases Windows logs to hinder investigations.

values.description:
GhostSec is a sophisticated hacktivist group that was initially formed in 2015 as an offshoot of the Anonymous hacktivist group to disrupt ISIS-related online propaganda and recently formed a hacking collective entity known as "The Five Families" that includes ThreatSec, Stormous, Blackforums, SiegedSec, GhostSec.

It has compromised multiple sectors including critical infrastructure, telecommunications, energy, defense in over 18 countries for achieving its ideological objectives. It uses a wide range of techniques for launching DDoS attack, exfiltrating lucrative data and defacement.

Source: Uptycs

values.description: Gold Dupont is a financially motivated threat group who has been in operation since at least 2018. The actor uses custom malware known as Vatet loader, PyXie Remote Access Tool, and Defray777 ransomware to gain initial access, perform reconnaissance, and exfiltrate and encrypt sensitive data. The group is also known to use various commodity malware and tools including Trickbot, Cobalt Strike, and Metasploit. The threat group targets various entities in the healthcare, education, government, and technology industries.

NoName057(16), also known as NoName05716, 05716nnm or Nnm05716, is a hacktivist group supporting Russia since March 2022. The NoName057(16) group is primarily focused on disrupting websites important to nations critical of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks act as the method to conduct such disruption efforts. Initial attacks focused on Ukrainian news websites, while later shifting to NATO associated targets.

Source: SentinelOne

Ransomhouse is a sophisticated ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group that emerged in late 2021. The group employs double extortion tactics, first encrypting victim networks then threatening to publish exfiltrated data if ransom demands are not met. Ransomhouse operates a Tor-based leak site to name-and-shame non-paying victims. The group tries to portray a professional image, offering personalized Onion chat links for negotiation and advice to bolster victims' security. Technically, Ransomhouse utilizes specialized tools like Babuk ransomware, and its variant Mario ransomware. It uses MrAgent to automate ransomware deployment across large environments. The group has targeted entities worldwide, with a focus on Western industries like technology and industrials.

The Chinese cyber espionage group UNC3886 demonstrates a sophisticated capability to compromise target systems through the exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities affecting firewall and virtualization technologies lacking Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) support. Their primary focus has been on defense, technology, and telecommunications organizations situated in the United States and the Asia-Pacific-Japan (APJ) regions.

values.description: UNC5221 is a threat actor that is known to leverage mutilple vulnerabilities to infect devices with custom malware. The group was found leveraging compromised out-of-support Cyberoam VPN appliances for command and control. The group, also tracked under the alias UTA0178, is suspected to be a Chinese nation-state-level threat actor.

values.description:
UNC5325 is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage operator that exploited CVE-2024-21893 to compromise Ivanti Connect Secure appliances. UNC5325 leveraged code from open-source projects, installed custom malware, and modified the appliance's settings in order to evade detection and attempt to maintain persistence.

Source: Mandiant

values.description:
The Water Curupira threat actor engages in campaigns to deploy backdoors like Cobalt Strike, ultimately facilitating Black Basta ransomware attacks. Initially involved in DarkGate and IcedID spam campaigns in the early weeks of the third quarter of 2023, the threat actor later shifted focus exclusively to Pikabot.

Source: Trend Micro
